description: OpenClaw plugin for Twitter search, follower exports, monitoring, media, and approved X automation through structured Xquik endpoints. Not affiliated with X Corp.
rules: Start with docs/context7-quickstarts.md for installation, authentication, API calls, MPP, monitors, webhooks, media, and fixes.
Use docs/context7-facts.md for identity, tools, credentials, MPP, endpoints, and approvals.
Use docs/context7-agent-guide.md for the concise agent contract.
Use docs/openclaw-setup.md for installation, configuration, runtime checks, polling, and fixes.
Use docs/agent-workflows.md for approvals, MPP, extraction, monitors, webhooks, and media.
Use openclaw.plugin.json for tool definitions, config, sensitive fields, and approvals.
Use package.json for package and OpenClaw install metadata.

TweetClaw is an OpenClaw plugin, not an MCP server. Link MCP users to https://docs.xquik.com/mcp/overview. Prefer OAuth 2.1. Clients that support custom bearer headers can use an Xquik API key; ChatGPT custom apps require OAuth.

If Codex reports Authorization server response missing required issuer: expected https://xquik.com, do not retry OAuth. Set XQUIK_API_KEY and bearer_token_env_var = "XQUIK_API_KEY" in Codex TOML. See https://docs.xquik.com/guides/troubleshooting#codex-oauth-issuer-validation-error and https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/31573.
Use tools.alsoAllow with explore and tweetclaw so users keep their normal OpenClaw tool profile.
Do not require credentials during installation. Live calls without them return setup guidance.
Treat API keys and signing keys as sensitive config; never print or commit them.
MPP mode is read-only and must not create writes, monitors, webhooks, uploads, DMs, or profile changes.
API-key prepaid credits cover 33 public paid-read routes without a subscription.
Direct MPP covers exactly 7 read routes: tweet lookup, user lookup, follower check, article lookup, trends, X trends, and community info.
Other paid reads require account-backed prepaid credits; media download is not MPP-eligible.
Use the ClawPack npm-pack workflow for ClawHub releases.
